sections.h2: Which Garrard County office answers which tax question?
sections.html:
The PVA owns the value, and the sheriff owns the bill. The county's own site stresses that the PVA neither sets rates nor collects, and the sheriff's page says the sheriff never assesses property, so an argument over the figure goes to one office and a question about paying goes to the other.

Both sit at 319 Stanford St. in Lancaster. The PVA answers at (859) 792-3291 on weekdays during the 8 to 4 day, and the sheriff's number is (859) 792-3591. The PVA is a state office with local reach, supervised by the Department of Revenue, and it values property at 100 percent of fair cash value as of January 1.

The sheriff collects for 28 taxing districts. They include the state, the county, school districts and special districts such as fire protection and libraries. Bills go out on October 1 every year with instructions on due dates, penalties, mortgage-company payment and ways to pay. The County Clerk, at 15 Public Square, Suite 5, records deeds and helps notify and collect on delinquent bills.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Garrard County?
sections.html:
Garrard County is in east-central Kentucky and has 230 square miles of land. Rolling Bluegrass country fills most of it, and the southeast corner near Cartersville falls in the Knobs. Lancaster, the seat and the only city, started as a cluster of log cabins in 1776, and the county was formed in 1796 from parts of Lincoln, Mercer and Madison counties, making it the 25th in the state.

Lexington is about 28 miles north. Beyond Lancaster, the named communities are Paint Lick, Bryantsville, Buckeye, Cartersville, Davis Town and Hyattsville, and every resident counted in 2020 lived in a rural area. Camp Dick Robinson, the first Federal base south of the Ohio River in the Civil War, was in the county. A tobacco heritage festival takes place every September, and voters ended the county's dry status on November 7, 2023.

The county has gained residents quickly, and many of them drive out of the county for work.

  • Population: 18,207 in the 2025 estimate, up 7.4 percent from 2020.
  • Typical home value in the 2020 to 2024 survey: $204,900.
  • Owner-occupied share: 79.9 percent, the highest among the four counties in this series.
  • Average commute: 33.1 minutes, the longest among the four.
  • New-home permits in 2025: 0.
  • Median gross rent: $794. Median household income: $63,087.

The 2020 census found 7,254 housing units with 9.2 percent vacant and 76.8 percent of occupied homes lived in by their owners. With no permits recorded in 2025, sales are mostly of existing houses and acreage.

sections.h2: When is the Garrard County bill due, and what is the discount?
sections.html:
The sheriff expects payment by December 31, and bills leave on October 1, so the early-payment window is about a month long. KRS 134.015 takes 2 percent off a bill paid in full by November 1, adds 5 percent in January and 10 percent after that.

If statewide mailing is delayed, the Department of Revenue can swap in a calendar of a month for the discount, a month at face and a month at the 5 percent charge. The tax is also the personal debt of whoever owned the property on January 1, which matters when a sale closes soon after New Year.

sections.h2: How much does a late Garrard County bill cost?
sections.html:
A lot more. After April 15 the sheriff moves every unpaid bill to the County Clerk and a lien is recorded. The Department of Revenue shows the growth with a $1,000 bill and an assumed 4 percent sheriff commission, so real totals will vary.

How a $1,000 delinquent bill grows at the clerk's office (source: Kentucky Department of Revenue)
StageTotal due
On transfer from the sheriff (penalty, add-on fee and commission included)$1,254.00
Paid within five business days of transfer$1,387.79
Paid after the first attorney notice$1,611.30
Paid in May, second month of interest$1,627.61
Paid in June, after newspaper advertising$1,659.90

Interest is 1 percent per month. A 30-day notice and a second notice come from the county attorney, and the clerk's sale is set 90 to 135 days after transfer. When a certificate sells to an outside buyer, you owe that buyer plus its additional fees.

sections.h2: How can a Garrard County owner appeal?
sections.html:
Meet with the PVA, then file with the County Clerk. The roll is open for 13 days beginning in early May, and the conference comes first. File by the end of the next business day after viewing closes.

A local board of assessment appeals then meets about four to five weeks later and rules on documented evidence: comparable listings, construction costs, photographs. It must give written reasons for a change. A paid representative must be an attorney, appraiser or another approved professional carrying your written authorization.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption for Garrard County owners?
sections.html:
Seniors and totally disabled owners can subtract $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Apply at the PVA on Stanford Street. At the county's typical home value of $204,900, the taxable amount would be $155,800.

To show age, bring a birth certificate, license or passport. A seller who has held the exemption should tell the PVA after closing so it ends at that address.

faqs.q: When do Garrard County tax bills go out?
faqs.a: They are mailed on October 1 each year, according to the Garrard County Sheriff. Payment in full by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount.

faqs.q: Who should I call if a Garrard County tax value looks wrong?
faqs.a: Call the Garrard County PVA at (859) 792-3291. The sheriff's office says it never assesses value and refers those questions to the PVA.

faqs.q: Where is the Garrard County sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: It is at 319 Stanford St. in Lancaster, KY 40444, with a phone at (859) 792-3591. The sheriff collects for 28 taxing districts.

faqs.q: What changes for Garrard County taxes still open on April 15?
faqs.a: The bill moves to the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a recorded lien. Interest of 1 percent per month starts, and clerk and attorney commissions follow.

faqs.q: What is the Garrard County homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, taken off the assessed value of a home owned by a senior or a totally disabled person.
